hypothesis: Actual Noah/Salih alignments map changed consonants to vowels, which were charged soft. Use the existing hard substitution cost across consonant/vowel pairs, retaining soft charges for ghunna and recitation marks. Predict three fewer checker-attributed and overall phone wrong calls with no clean or studio regression.
author: Yazin

hypothesisHistory.hypothesis: The phoneme alignment maps a changed consonant to a vowel and discounts it as a soft edit, so Noah/Salih substitutions have only one hard edit and never become candidates. Count a consonant-vowel replacement at its actual substitution cost whenever either side is a consonant. Predict three fewer checker-attributed and overall wrong calls; preserve clean recitation and studio without lowering acoustic support thresholds.
hypothesisHistory.reason: The broad either-consonant prototype introduced four clean-fixture assertion failures by hardening ghunna/recitation-mark changes. Narrow to vowel/consonant substitutions before the first practice score.
